paragraphs: 2NDNATURE sells stormwater software built on GIS, aimed at streamlining compliance, asset tracking and reporting. Buyers fall into two camps, those tackling MS4 permit requirements and those advancing corporate water stewardship. Two products carry that work, 2NFORM and Rainsteward, both pitched at streamlining compliance and showing measurable results.

2NFORM is organized around municipal permit programs, covering post-construction, industrial and commercial, and illicit discharge detection and elimination. In Oceanside it was connected to the city's existing Esri-based GIS and met local security and IT standards. For longer-range planning the company built a Stormwater Asset Management Model that serves as a decision-making tool. Fed with the storm sewer system and local costs, it lets a city explore how twenty years of asset management would affect the health of that system. Rainsteward points the other way, at owners trying to cut costs and get more value out of stormwater investments.

The customers shown are city stormwater programs; Oceanside had nine separate systems tracking inspections and compliance tasks before it changed course. Salinas is described as a Phase I MS4 with a population exceeding 150,000. That city worked with 2NDNATURE to develop a comprehensive Asset Improvement Plan. Private owners appear too: a real estate company called Reveler implemented Rainsteward in a series of six steps.
